newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ looks for non-interest income growth.
newsitem.headline: ANZ looks for non-interest income growth.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd said on Wednesday it was looking to continued growth in lending assets and increased non-interest income to offset the continuing downward prssure on interest margines.

"The group will also build on the progress made in the first half to improve efficiency with the financial benefits of the changes underway becoming more apparent in the second half of the year," the bank said.
ANZ chairman Charles Goode said the result was sound and was made under increasingly competitive conditions.
"Pressure on interest margins was offset by asset growth, increased non-interest income and cost control," he said.
"Favourable credit conditions continue with a low doubtful debt charge and a further fall in non-accrual loans," he said.
The bank said its Tier One capital adequacy ratio remained steady at 6.7 percent.
"As we have said previously, 1997 is the year in which we are starting to see the benefits flowing from our recent strategic initiatives," Goode said.
